transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-06-30
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Recording: yes
- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CS briefly), Priya Patel (Starlight CISO), Daniel Gomez (Head of Infrastructure), Maya Chen (Compliance), Ethan Li (DevOps)

Auto-summary: quick SOC2/ISO posture check, trust center access, controls mapping, encryption and KMS discussion, RBAC/SSO and audit log retention. Next steps captured at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Marco, our solutions engineer, and Aisha from CS will drop in for a minute. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya: Doing good, thanks. We're, uh, mostly focused on validating your SOC 2 and ISO posture before we move to a pilot.
[00:12] Daniel: Yeah, and we want to understand the controls mapping and what artifacts you can share. Also, curious about trust center access and SSO.
[00:20] Lena: Perfect. Marco will run through the technical controls and audit log story, and I'll cover the reports and trust center. Quick ask: can we confirm this call is a security-only review, yes?
[00:28] Priya: Yes, security/compliance focussed.
[00:31] Marco: Alright, jumping in. High level, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates, our trust center houses evidence and control descriptions. For infra we support RBAC via SSO/SAML, audit logs with configurable retention, and encryption at rest using customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations.
[00:49] Maya: Can you clarify who holds the keys in each deployment mode? Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[00:55] Marco: Sure - in hosted we offer default Redwood-managed keys, but customers can opt into bringing their own KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure KeyVault) for tenant-level CMKs. For Dedicated, you can provision a dedicated key ring and we can integrate with customer KMS. For Private/VPC on-prem we support HSM/KMS entirely customer-managed. There was a doc called, uh, "bring-your-own-kms" in our trust center.
[01:20] Priya: And the SOC 2 report - does it include the controls mapping to ISO? We need to run a gap analysis.
[01:27] Lena: The raw reports are SOC 2 Type II with control descriptions. We also maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our SOC 2 controls to ISO 27001 clauses - Marco will share that. It's in the trust center as well, but we'll give you a direct copy.
[01:39] Ethan: What's the retention on audit logs by default? We need 12 months for certain telemetry.
[01:44] Marco: Default in hosted is 90 days for the UI logs, but audit logs for compliance - like API access and admin actions - can be exported and retained longer. We support configurable retention up to 7 years via the dedicated logging export to customer S3 or a SIEM integration. For dedicated and private you have more direct control over retention.
[02:03] Priya: Are the audit logs tamper-evident?
[02:06] Marco: We support append-only export to S3 with object lock if you want immutability, and we can provide signed ingestion timestamps. It's not a blockchain, but we do provide integrity proofs by signed digests for exported batches.
[02:17] Daniel: Ok that's helpful. About trust center access - what's the onboarding process? We need read-only access for compliance folks.
[02:23] Lena: Simple - I can request a read-only trust center invite for your domain. It leverages SSO, so your SAML IdP will control access. We'll map groups to RBAC roles.
[02:33] Maya: Do you support SCIM provisioning?
[02:35] Marco: Yes, SCIM for user provisioning is supported and recommended for larger teams.
[02:39] [00:03:40] (note - timestamp typo in transcript generator)
[02:40] Priya: Great. A couple of things: we need proof of encryption in transit and at rest, plus key rotation policy. Where do we find those artifacts?
[02:50] Lena: The whitepaper and key mgmt section in the trust center. We have a KMS/hsm architecture doc that outlines rotation cadence (90 days for CMK rotation is typical but configurable) and TLS mTLS for internal comms. We'll attach those.
[03:04] Ethan: For pilot, if we want to keep data in US-East only and have logs sent to our S3 in us-east-2, is that straightforward?
[03:12] Marco: Yep - region pinning and log export endpoints are supported. For hosted, we maintain region residency options and can route your tenant to a US region. For Dedicated or Private, you control placement.
[03:21] Priya: There's often confusion over 'redwood dedicated' vs 'private', can you clarify?
[03:25] Marco: Sure - Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud with tenant isolation and dedicated GPU pools. Private means the control plane is customer-managed and can be run in your VPC or on-prem; it gives you network-level isolation and full control of keys and logs. Sometimes people call Dedicated "dedicate" in notes, so yeah naming slips.
[03:43] Daniel: Are penetration test reports available? We require recent external pentest summary.
[03:47] Lena: We have a 3rd-party pentest summary and vulnerability management metrics in the trust center. Sensitive findings are redacted, but we provide a summary and remediation timelines.
[03:55] Maya: For SOC 2, do you map CC6 and CC7 etc to specific operational controls?
[03:59] Marco: Yes - our controls mapping doc shows control IDs, test procedures, and where evidence lives. We'll give you an annotated spreadsheet mapping SOC criteria to our ISO clauses too.
[04:10] [00:04:10] Marco: On RBAC, Redwood supports role-based roles at the org, project, and route/endpoint level. You can create custom roles for e.g., "audit-only" or "model-admin". We integrate these roles with SSO groups.
[04:24] Priya: Any limitations on SAML assertions size or session length?
[04:28] Marco: Defaults align with industry norms; session length configurable via SAML assertion TTLs and session policies. We can align to your SSO settings.
[04:36] Lena: Quick commercial note - often customers choose Dedicated when they have strict retention and residency needs to simplify compliance. But Private gives maximum control; tradeoffs are ops overhead.
[04:47] Priya: Understood. Could you confirm the evidence we can get for control testing - like change logs, config diff, etc?
[04:53] Marco: We can export admin change logs, deployments history, config snapshots, and network access logs. For Dedicated/Private you get more granular logs and direct access. For hosted we ingest and can export sanitized snapshots.
[05:05] Daniel: For the controls mapping, will you include which artifacts correspond to which tests so our auditors can consume them directly?
[05:11] Marco: Yes, the mapping includes artifact names, location in trust center, and typical retention windows.
[05:17] Maya: Any SOC 2 exceptions in the last year we should be aware of?
[05:20] Lena: No material exceptions - we note minor process findings in the past year, all remediated. We'll include a one-page exceptions summary in the package.
[05:29] Priya: About network segmentation - do you have diagrams showing control plane separation from customer data plane?
[05:34] Marco: Yep, network diagrams and architecture docs are in the trust center. For Dedicated we show VPC peering options and egress controls.
[05:42] Ethan: Does Redwood support customer-managed logging endpoints with TLS mutual auth?
[05:46] Marco: Yes - mutual TLS is supported for log endpoints and we can configure client certs.
[05:52] Priya: How fast can you provide the reports? We're trying to present to our audit committee next week.
[05:58] Lena: We can send SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs as PDF within 2 business days and grant trust center read-only access within 24-48 hours once we have the list of users.
[06:09] Daniel: Sounds good. A follow-up: for KMS integration, is Redwood making API calls to customer KMS directly or via a proxy? We want to ensure we own key access logs.
[06:18] Marco: Typically we call the KMS APIs in your account or use a cross-account role; logs of key usage remain in your KMS audit logs. For cases where a proxy is used in Dedicated setups we document the flow.
[06:29] Priya: Is there an SOC 2 scope document listing in-scope services and exclusions?
[06:33] Lena: Yes, scope doc included in the pack. We'll highlight service boundaries and third-party subprocessors.
[06:39] Maya: Any support for encrypted backups for model artifacts?
[06:43] Marco: Backups are encrypted at rest. For dedicated/private we can configure customer-managed keys for backups too.
[06:49] [00:06:49] (Marco clarifies some acronyms)
[06:50] Priya: Ok, a few nitty-gritty items for our auditors: sample user provisioning logs, examples of least privilege role configs, and a recent vulnerability remediations timeline. Can those be provided?
[07:02] Lena: Yes, those are standard asks - we'll include anonymized examples and timelines.
[07:07] Daniel: On data residency, are there any services that still replicate metadata cross-region for availability? We need guarantees that ePHI is not leaving region unless failover.
[07:17] Marco: Primary data tenancy will stay in region; for some global infra metadata (health checks, routing metadata) we may have minimal metadata outside region but not ePHI. We'll provide the data residency whitepaper and explicit guarantees for ePHI.
[07:31] Priya: Good. One more - do you provide an audit log API so we can pull logs programmatically?
[07:35] Marco: Yes, we have an Audit Log API and integrations with common SIEMs. We'll hand over API docs and sample scripts.
[07:43] Lena: Ok, we are close on time, quick recap of next steps?
[07:48] Priya: Please send the reports and trust center invite; Marco send the mapping; we'll confirm residency and schedule the VPC deep dive.
[07:55] Lena: Great - I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the VPC deep dive once we get Ethan's availability.
[07:59] Maya: Thanks everyone - this was helpful.
[08:02] Lena: Thanks all. We'll get those artifacts over.

End of recording.

Attachments referenced: trust center link (invite pending), SOC 2 Type II PDF, ISO 27001 certificate, controls_mapping_starlight.xlsx, kms_architecture.pdf, audit_log_api_docs.md

Notes on transcription fidelity: occasional mis-hearings ("Dedicate" for Dedicated, "KMS/HSM" sometimes transcribed as "KMS H-M-S"), timestamps approximate.
